# Lumen

Lumen is a free browser tool that checks which EU AI Act Article 50 transparency labels your AI deployment needs. It runs entirely in the browser (no data leaves the device).

## Key facts (verified 13 August 2026)

- Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) became applicable on 2 August 2026.
- Article 50 transparency duties apply from that date — no transition.
- Art. 50(1): chatbots and AI assistants must inform users they are interacting with AI (unless obvious).
- Art. 50(2): AI-generated image/audio/video must be marked as artificially generated in a machine-readable format.
- Art. 50(3): deepfakes must be labelled; public-interest deepfakes disclosed at first use.
- Art. 50(4): AI text published to inform the public must be disclosed, unless human-reviewed with editorial responsibility.
- Fines: up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover (Art. 99).
- Content generated before 2 August 2026 is not labelled retroactively.

## Pricing

- Free: label check + checklist + fine exposure.
- Pro (14 USD one-time, crypto via NOWPayments): printable label PDF, disclosure copy, Art. 50 readiness checklist, permanent unlock.

## Not advice

Lumen is an educational tool based on Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. It is not legal advice. Editorial responsibility: attenciona (Holding), Spain.
